concepts.definition: Effortful practice designed to improve a specific aspect of performance, with a goal just beyond current ability and immediate feedback.
Repetition without specific goals or feedback.
A popular claim that a fixed number of hours makes an expert, which the original research does not support.

questions.q: Why might deliberate practice explain so little variance in professional performance?
questions.a: Professional performance is hard to measure, tasks vary, feedback is late, and few professionals practice deliberately at all.

questions.q: How did the 2019 replication of the violin study differ from the original result?
questions.a: Practice still explained about a quarter of the variance, but the best violinists had not practiced more than the good ones, unlike the 1993 claim.

questions.q: Turn "get better at writing" into a deliberate practice task.
questions.a: For example: rewrite ten headlines for one article in 20 minutes, compare with expert examples and get comments on two weaknesses.
